targetReport.title: Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System (HS)
targetReport.description: The multipurpose international product nomenclature developed by the World Customs Organization: more than 5,000 commodity groups, each identified by a six-digit code. The commodity-side counterpart to the industry classifications already in this corpus — national trade statistics, including Canada's, are coded to it, with countries adding digits beyond six for tariff and statistical detail.
targetReport.cadence_note: The WCO's Harmonized System Committee 'prepares amendments updating the HS every 5 – 6 years' — editions 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.rule: The WCO prepares amendments updating the HS nomenclature every 5-6 years through the Review Sub-Committee and HS Committee; the HS Convention provides a two-and-one-half-year implementation period after adoption before a new edition enters into force (six months for reservations, two years for correlation tables/translation/legislative updates). The HS2022 edition entered into force 1 January 2022; the next edition, originally planned as HS2027, was pushed back one year due to COVID-19-related delays and will be HS2028, entering into force 1 January 2028.
release_schedule.note: This is a periodic amendment/nomenclature update, not a recurring data report with dated calendar entries. The WCO's own site frames it as a 5-6 year revision cycle governed by the HS Convention's implementation timeline rather than a fixed calendar. A further, more fundamental revision (HS2033) is already being planned as a follow-on cycle.

targetReport.description: The State Council regulation governing China's decennial agricultural census, promulgated in August 2006. It fixes the census on a ten-year cycle in years ending in 6, sets the standard reference point at 24:00 on 31 December of the census year, and defines the census objects (rural households, urban agricultural production households, agricultural production and operation units, villagers' committees and township governments) and its industry scope (crop cultivation, forestry, animal husbandry, fishery and agricultural support activities).
